thread:
emily (Support): FYI SomniPay is reporting repeated 429s every minute for the last ~2 hours. Spikes all line up at the top of the minute (:00). They're on hosted API eu-west1, model=redwood-v1, endpoint=/v1/generate. sample request id: req_abc123

sam (SRE): Looking. Do we have any X-RateLimit headers from their failed responses? Also what RPM/TPM do they claim to be sending?

emily (Support): They sent a dump: 
X-RateLimit-Limit: 120
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 60
They reported ~180 RPM during peak minute windows, concurrency ~6 from their workers.

jon (Eng): 120 RPM looks like a per-minute cap, so 180 would exceed it. TPM might also be relevant depending on payload size. Can SRE pull gateway logs around :00 for their org_id?

logs-bot: extracted snippet from gateway logs for org=org_somni around 2026-03-17T12:00:00Z:
[12:00:00.001] req=req_abc120 status=200
[12:00:00.002] req=req_abc121 status=200
[12:00:00.003] req=req_abc122 status=429 frame=ratecap-service
[12:00:00.004] req=req_abc123 status=429 frame=ratecap-service
[12:00:00.004] req=req_abc124 status=429 frame=ratecap-service
(large cluster of identical timestamps at :00 and :30)

sam (SRE): Logs show a tight cluster of requests with identical second timestamps. This looks like scheduling collision (many workers running at top-of-minute). Ratecap service returns 429 immediately once bucket exhausted. Also saw cache miss briefly at :00 which may have increased upstream load.

lina (CSM): SomniPay says their jobs run on minute boundaries and they can't change schedule easily right now. They asked if we can do a temporary quota bump while they implement a fix.

jon (Eng): Short-term mitigation options:
- Temporary quota bump/reserved capacity for their org (fast but manual)
- Recommend jitter + exponential backoff on client side
- If payloads identical, enable request folding/caching to collapse duplicates

sam (SRE): I can apply a transient reserved-capacity override for 24h (2x RPM) to buy time. Need product signoff.

maya (Product): Approved for a 24h trial increase for org_somni. Emily, please get customer consent and confirm scope.

emily (Support): Customer agreed to the 24h bump. Proceeding.

sam (SRE): Applied temporary 2x RPM quota to org_somni at 12:05 UTC. Monitoring dashboards now.

dashbot: metric event: org_somni.rpm spike at 12:00 -> before bump peak=185 RPM, after bump peak=183 but 429s dropped to <1% within 2 minutes of applying override.

jon (Eng): Client guidance to share with SomniPay: sample jitter/backoff snippet:
```js
// stagger top-of-minute cron
const jitter = Math.floor(Math.random() * 30000); // up to 30s
setTimeout(() => callGenerateAPI(), jitter);
// simple backoff
async function callWithBackoff(req, attempt=0) {
  try { return await fetch(req); }
  catch (err) {
    if (attempt > 5) throw err;
    await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, Math.pow(2, attempt) * 1000 + Math.random()*1000));
    return callWithBackoff(req, attempt+1);
  }
}
```

emily (Support): Shared the jitter + backoff guide and asked them to progressively ramp traffic down to even intervals. Created ticket SUP-4829 to track remediation and quota request.

sam (SRE): Action items: add postmortem note about 'top-of-minute cron collision'; consider adding a smoothing policy that enforces per-second soft caps to reduce minute-boundary storms. Also recommend exposing per-second rate headers for easier debugging.

emily (Support): Thanks team :thumbsup: I'll close the handoff when the 24h window finishes and SomniPay confirms no further 429s. Leaving here for follow-up (SUP-4829).
